related_questions.question: How to relieve COVID symptoms fast?

text_blocks.snippet: To relieve COVID-19 symptoms quickly, focus on rest, hydration, and over-the-counter medications for fever and pain. Consider antiviral treatments if eligible and prescribed by a doctor. Early treatment, ideally within 5 days of symptom onset, is crucial.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on rest, hydration, and over-the-counter medications for fever and pain

list.snippet: Rest: Prioritize sleep and avoid strenuous activity to allow your body to recover.
Hydration: Drink plenty of fluids like water, clear broths, or electrolyte drinks to stay hydrated and replace fluids lost through fever or other symptoms.
Over-the-counter medications: Use acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) for fever, body aches, and headaches.

Antiviral treatments: If you're at high risk for severe illness, consider antiviral medications like Paxlovid, which can reduce the severity and duration of COVID-19. Consult your doctor immediately to see if you're eligible.
Monitor your health: Track your symptoms and seek medical attention if you experience severe symptoms like difficulty breathing, persistent chest pain, confusion, or bluish lips or face.
Isolate: Stay away from others to prevent spreading the virus.
Masks: Wear a mask when around others to minimize transmission.
Good hygiene: Frequently wash your hands with soap and water.
Nutritious diet: Eat healthy foods to support your immune system.

How does contact tracing work? Contact tracing is a system that has been used for decades to stop infectious diseases. A contact is anyone who has had direct physical contact or is within one metre for at least 15 minutes with an infected person. Even if that person does not have symptoms. This applies to anyone who has had contact from two days before a person gets sick until 14 days afterwards. Or from the 14 days when an asymptomatic case tested positive. Once you are confirmed as a contact, you'll be asked to go into quarantine which means to separate yourself from others and to monitor your health for any signs of illness. The monitoring ends on the fourteenth day from your last contact with the person infected with COVID-19.
